title: AidPage Atlas — rule-based, rank-free multi-lens profiles of Korean municipalities (v1.7) with national aid thresholds, recorded outcomes and evacuation access
description: Rule-based typology of 256 Korean municipal units (si/gun/gu): natural hazards (flood history, landslide/slope, coastal contact, drought zones), a social hazard (traffic), unordered vulnerability traits, and ordinance holdings. National top-quartile thresholds within the same unit class; no composite score or ranking. v1.4 adds the national recovery-aid threshold layer (fiscal-capacity bands, Regulation art. 5①, in force 2024-11-19) and recorded outcomes from the Disaster Yearbook 2012–2024. v1.4.1 (2026-09-17) restores Jeongeup-si (52180), which was missing from v1.4 (255 units); merged-unit specification is now 230. Sensitivity specifications (p70/p80, 230 units) shipped for review. v1.5 (2026-10-11) adds an evacuation-access layer (residents whose shortest walk to designated temporary housing crosses a deep past-flood record; residents more than 60 min away at 48 m/min; OSM path network, H3 cells, population-weighted), a 227-unit reporting specification, and fills facility gaps in districts created by the 2026-07-01 reorganisation; types unchanged. Files: data/ref/sgg_types.json, sgg_threshold.json, sgg_type_specs.json, sgg_ordin.json, sgg_access.json; viewer: atlas.html. v1.7 (2026-10-14) adds a reference line under every indicator bar citing the statute, agency definition or national value it rests on (only two indicators have official thresholds applicable to municipal values: ageing stages 7/14/20% and the MOIS foreign-resident concentration rule), a same-type peer list, an 'all three nearest shelters' evacuation line, unifies the all-records evacuation share with the deep-record rule, restores Jeongeup's traffic value (types v1.4.2) and corrects two labels (registered disability; basic livelihood eligibility). Data are provided on request with a data-use agreement.
